title: How to avoid paying the TV Licence fee legally
full_text:

notes.note: You need a TV Licence to watch live TV or BBC iPlayer on any device, including a battery-powered iPhone. A device used only on its own batteries away from home is covered only if your home address is already licensed, not if neither property has one.
notes.claim: Watching television on a battery-powered iPhone running on its battery does not require a TV licence and can be done anywhere, because the licence relates to a property not a person, including at a friend's house that has no licence.
notes.context_quote: If you watch television on an iPhone and it is running on its battery, you do not need a TV license. So you can watch it wherever you are. The license relates to the property, not to the person. So you could be at a friend's house who hasn't got a license and you can watch a battery powered device without a license.
notes.context_paragraph: If you watch television on an iPhone and it is running on its battery, you do not need a TV license. So you can watch it wherever you are. The license relates to the property, not to the person. So you could be at a friend's house who hasn't got a license and you can watch a battery powered device without a license.

sources.explanation: Confirms using iPlayer needs a licence.

sources.quote: You need a TV Licence to watch or record programmes on a TV, computer or other device as they're broadcast, and to watch on-demand BBC programmes on iPlayer
sources.explanation: States the basic licence requirement covers live broadcast on any device and on-demand iPlayer.

sources.quote: watch or record live TV on any channel or service
sources.explanation: Confirms live TV on any channel/service needs a licence.

sources.explanation: Shows battery-powered use away from home relies on using the other address's existing licence, not being licence-free.

sources.quote: whether you're watching live TV on a television, computer, tablet, games console, smartphone or any other device, you'll need to be covered by a TV licence.
sources.explanation: Directly says live TV on any device including smartphone needs a licence.

sources.quote: For example, watching live TV on a phone requires a licence (though if you already have a licence at your home address you won't need an additional one for a [mobile device used outside the home](#needtoknow-14)).
sources.explanation: Directly says watching live TV on a phone requires a licence, with home licence covering outside use.

sources.quote: Additionally, if you pay for a licence at home, it'll cover you on a mobile device outside of your home too (subject to certain conditions – see the below point on [mobile devices](https://www.moneysavingexpert.com/broadband-and-tv/tv-licence/#needtoknow-14)).
sources.explanation: Shows outside-home mobile coverage depends on paying for a home licence.

sources.quote: Your "out-of-term address" (for example, your parents' or guardians' address) is covered by a TV Licence.
sources.explanation: Shows battery exception requires the home/out-of-term address already be licensed.

sources.quote: You only watch TV on a device that's powered solely by its own internal batteries (like a smartphone, tablet or laptop).
sources.explanation: Shows the exception applies to battery-only devices like smartphones.
